title: The Aftermath Frame — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of The Aftermath Frame's rich face, its first round at Study tier: the swing solver laid open up to a check of the page's numbers and of where its blade meets the wood, the comic gain made draggable up to a check that fails if the gain reaches the motion (run on a port and on BLUELINE's impact tool in Blender), and two of BLUELINE's proofs laid beside the lines they prove, with the fingerprint of the words each was made against. The grain is the page's own two ## sections. I grow when the page is rewritten or the tool changes; I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: For BLUELINE's scroll, not this page's text (challenger's routing). The page's numbers hold (the solver gives 132.897°, 23.195 rad/s, 32.937 m/s; the impact tool's own code in Blender agrees), but the chop they come from runs its blade through the column before the contact. With the solver's 1.42 m reach the blade enters the top of the tool's column at 197.3 ms of the 250 ms swing, after 73.6° of 132.9°, and cuts down through it for the rest; the authored contact sits 22.1 cm in front of the wood, so v_c (20.2 m/s) is read in air, and where the impact-pose blade enters the wood it moves at 25.8 m/s. Rising enters at 189 ms (66.8° of 134.4°), side at 243 ms; both contacts are 24.1 cm off the wood; the rising tip is below z = 0, where the tool plants the feet, until 190 ms. The drawn sword is another blade: 0.36 m from the posed hands, 36° off the model's, ending 17 cm short of the wood. The challenger adds two: the page's 33 m/s tip belongs to a 1.42 m reach that is never drawn (the drawn sword's end, 0.910 m from the pivot, moves at 21.1 m/s); and a contact moved onto the wood at the same height, (1.14, 0.02, 1.06), gives 128.3° / 22.4 rad/s / 31.8 m/s, so a fix would fail the page's three numbers. Measured in the tool's own scene in Blender 5.1.2 (tool check.py), confirmed by the challenger's numpy rebuild and Blender re-run. A tension left for Loudon, not resolved: finding the contact is cheap geometry, but it moves the tool toward fidelity, against the BLUELINE baton's line that physical fidelity is "still the WRONG direction". This page's own share is offer 2.

offers.section: The method — model the action as a rotation
offers.what: The contact is authored, not found; and name what the figures rest on. The solver authors pivot, windup direction, contact, pivot-to-tip reach (1.42 m), time to impact (0.25 s) and the exponent of θ(t) = Δθ·(t/T)^k (2.5); the axis (d_windup × d_impact) and Δθ are derived, where the text lists the axis and θ(t) as authored and does not list the contact. ω at impact is Δθ·k/T and the tip that × 1.42, so at T = 300 ms the page's 23 rad/s becomes 19.3. Proposed: "(an overhead chop: pivot at the upper chest, 1.42 m to the tip, 0.25 s to impact — Δθ 133°, ω 23 rad/s, tip 33 m/s)" and "{pivot, windup direction, contact, θ(t) with a peak-at-impact ω, blade as a rigid body}; the axis and the amplitude are derived, and the contact is authored, not found." Confirmed by the challenger.

"a boolean wound removes material exactly where the blade passed": in the tool (and session 10, whose report says "the blade's swept volume") the kerf is the drawn sword at its impact pose, widened to 0.11 × 0.05 m and run 0.7 m on (1.06 m long, from the posed hands), so it removes where the drawn sword lies at impact, not where the modelled blade passed; that blade passed through the column's top from 197 ms on and none of that path is cut (Blender, the tool's own scene). Proposed: "a boolean wound removes a slot along the blade at the moment of impact, and the shards spray from that gash."

Demoted from claim-change on the challenger's read: a falling mean-direction length is what spread means, and the split held (v_c bit-identical at gain 1 and 10 on the port, identical across the tool's punch 0, 1 and 3.9 in Blender; a copy with the gain wired into time-to-impact fails both). What spread costs is each shard's aim: coherence 0.886 at gain 1, 0.752 at the tool's heroic spread 1.8, 0.642 at super 2.6, 0.257 at 10; a single shard sits 27°, 40°, 49° and 75° off v_c on average; the mean stays within about 10° of v_c at every gain. Optional, if Loudon wants it said: after "never the motion", "— though the wider the spray, the less each shard points back at the swing." Untested on any reader.

"take their direction … from the real contact velocity": the shards burst along v_c plus the wound's outward normal and a lift. In the tool's locked arc spray (0.2 × normal) the mean shard flies about 10° off v_c (10.3° at spread 1, 9.3° at the heroic 1.8); in session 10's build, the impact proof the page names (1.5 × normal, run at spread 1.8, build_impact.py:79), 42.9° off. The spread gain moves that mean a few degrees toward v_c (10.3° at 1 to about 7° at 10), since the cone opens across v_c rather than around the burst. Proposed: "from the real contact velocity and the wound's outward face". Confirmed by the challenger with the 42.9° correction.

pieces.title: a swing is a rotation · five steps
pieces.caption: **The page's numbers, derived and held to the page; then the question they take for granted.** One blade turning about one pivot, its angle on a schedule, its speed peaking at impact, every point's velocity. Last, two checks with their rules stated first. At the solver's 1.42 m reach, 250 ms to impact and exponent 2.5, which the page doesn't name, the chop gives 132.9°, 23.2 rad/s and 32.9 m/s, so the page's 133, 23 and 33 pass; this confirms the page copied the solver, and moving the time to impact fails it. The real test: at that reach the blade is inside the column 53 ms before the authored contact, which sits 22 cm in front of the wood. A control built to pass, passes.

pieces.title: three swings, one solver · BLUELINE session 9
pieces.caption: Chop, side slash, rising cut: one solver, three authored vectors each (pivot, windup, contact). The rotation axis, the contact velocity and every consequence re-aim on their own: speed-lines down into the contact, across, and down behind a blade that came from below. Session 9 has no wound yet; the column is whole, and in the chop tile the drawn sword stops short of it. Clay render, Blender 5.1.2.

verdicts.file: The Aftermath Frame — rich — a swing is a rotation.html
verdicts.why: Walks up from one angle to a wood check that fails, and the failure holds: rebuilt independently and in Blender, 197.3 ms, contact 22.1 cm off the wood. The page-number check is only a transcription check. Note: the caption should name the 1.42 m, 250 ms and k 2.5 the page doesn't.

Caption only: 'speed-lines down into the wound' is wrong, because session 9 has no wound (no kerf in build_swings.py; session-10 report: 'Sessions 7–9 left the column a static, undeformed cylinder'). Say 'into the contact'.

pieces.by: the impact tool's debris block, ported · checked against Blender
pieces.title: the gain and the motion · five steps
pieces.caption: **Turn the comic gain to 10 and the swing does not move: tested, with a null that fails.** From the one arrow everything reads (v_c), to the shards and the air read from it, to a gain you can drag. Last, the whole frame at gain 1 and gain 10: v_c, ω and the tip are bit-identical while shards and streaks grow tenfold; wire the gain into the swing's speed and the same check fails. The tool itself, run in Blender, gives the same answer across its punch dial. What the gain does change is each shard's aim: 27° off v_c on average at gain 1, 75° at 10, while their mean stays within about 10°.

pieces.title: the wound and the arc speed-lines · BLUELINE session 10
pieces.caption: The boolean wound and the speed-lines traced along the swing's own arc, stopping short of the blade. The wound is a slot cut along the drawn sword at the moment of impact, widened and run on through the column — not, as the text says, where the blade passed; see the offers. The shards are spawned from it. Clay render, Blender 5.1.2.

verdicts.why: The test and null hold (Blender re-run: v_c −18.56 vs −188.57 m/s in the leaky copy). Fix three sentences: step 1's 'the only thing ... allowed to read' (the wake reads the whole path), step 4's '0.6 to 3.4' (it is 3.2), and 'little left to run it from' (the mean stays 6.7° off v_c and the swoosh holds the arc).
The right proof beside 'The impact is real too', and the caption is accurate about the build. Note: label its disagreement with the text ('not, as the text says, where the blade passed').
